sections.html:
Bettendorf is a city in Scott County on the Mississippi River, next to Davenport and across the river from Moline, East Moline and Rock Island, Illinois. It is one of the five Quad Cities.

The city covers about 22.4 square miles, of which 21.3 are land and 1.1 are water, at an elevation of roughly 666 feet. The 2020 census counted 39,102 residents, which ranked Bettendorf 15th in Iowa. A 2022 estimate put the figure at 39,548, up from 33,217 in 2010. The median age in 2020 was 39.9.

The city council has five wards and two at-large seats. Property in the city is assessed through the Scott County Assessor, since only Davenport runs its own assessor.

sections.h2: How did Bettendorf get its name and its start?
sections.html:
The land came to the United States after the Black Hawk War, through the 1832 Black Hawk Purchase from the Sac and Fox. It was then part of Wisconsin Territory.

Settlers founded two villages, Lilienthal and Gilbert, which merged into the town of Gilbert. Most residents were German immigrants. Around 1900 the town gave William and Joseph Bettendorf 70 acres of riverfront land so they could move their iron wagon business from Davenport. In 1903 the town of 440 people incorporated and took the brothers' name.

The city's later growth came from the riverfront industries described below, and the population rose from 33,217 in 2010 to 39,102 in 2020.

Manufacturing, the river and the casino industry have each had a turn. In the late 1940s the Aluminum Company of America chose Riverdale, an enclave of Bettendorf, for what was then described as the world's largest aluminum mill. It created thousands of jobs and fueled population growth.

Riverboat casinos debuted in Bettendorf on April 1, 1991, founded by Bernard Goldstein, who later founded Isle of Capri Casinos. The Quad Cities Waterfront Convention Center opened in 2009. The city owns it and Isle of Capri operates it. Alter Companies, run by the Goldstein family, operates scrap metal, barge and towboat businesses on the waterfront.

Wikipedia does not list current major employers for Bettendorf, so this page does not either. Scott Community College in Riverdale and an Upper Iowa University Quad Cities Center are the higher-education sites in the city.

Two districts serve the city, and the address decides which one. That is worth checking before you describe a house to a buyer.

DistrictArea covered
Bettendorf Community School DistrictMost of central, northern and western Bettendorf; operates Bettendorf High School
Pleasant Valley Community School DistrictEastern Bettendorf, plus Pleasant Valley, Riverdale and LeClaire

Edison Academy is a consortium alternative high school in downtown Bettendorf. Private schools include Rivermont Collegiate, Lourdes Catholic School and Morning Star Academy.

sections.h2: How do the I-74 bridge and river flooding affect Bettendorf sellers?
sections.html:
The I-74 Bridge ties Bettendorf to Moline, Illinois. The original twin spans opened in 1935 and 1959, and a $1.2 billion replacement project that began in July 2017 was completed in 2021. It turned Grant Street near I-74 into a two-way street with three lanes in each direction.

Flooding is the other local fact a seller should know. Wikipedia reports that the city lies along the river and experiences frequent flooding and annual stormwater runoff. A 2000 study of 14 drainageways found 169 inlets inadequate for heavy rainfall, with Crow, Pigeon and Spencer creeks named as problem areas.

  • If the house is near one of those creeks, expect questions about basement water.
  • Keep any repair receipts for sump pumps, drain tile or waterproofing.
  • Ask your insurer for the flood zone designation before you list the property.

A cash buyer purchases the house in its present condition, wet basement included, which spares you from repairing something a lender-financed buyer would ask you to fix first.

sections.h2: What is the Bettendorf rental license rule?
sections.html:
Landlords in Bettendorf must hold a current rental registration and pass a rental inspection before renting residential property. The registration goes on file with the City Clerk before an inspection can be scheduled, and the city offers an online form.

An inspection certificate is issued once the structure is found to comply with the city code. To schedule, email CodeEnforcement@bettendorf.org or call the code enforcement hotline at (563) 344-4064 and leave a message. City Hall is at 1609 State Street, Bettendorf, IA 52722, and the main number is (563) 344-4000.

The program page does not state the inspection cycle, the fees or what happens when a rental property is sold, so ask the city or read the rental housing code before closing. If you are selling a rented house, tell us at the start so we can find out what the city needs.

sections.h2: How do Scott County tax payments work for a Bettendorf owner?
sections.html:
Bettendorf owners pay property tax to the Scott County Treasurer, which collects in two equal installments due September 30 and March 31. Taxes are certified in July or August.

The Treasurer has two offices in Davenport: the Administrative Center at 600 W. 4th St. and the General Store at 902 W. Kimberly Rd., Suite 6D. You can pay online by e-check for $0.25 or by credit card at 2.25%. Cash and checks carry no fee at the counter, and debit cards at the counter cost $2.00 per transaction. Interest starts the first business day after a due date.

If taxes stay unpaid, they are published in June and sold at the tax sale on the third Monday of June. A seller with an open installment can clear it at closing, but do not wait until the publication date to ask for a payoff figure.

sections.h2: What should a Bettendorf seller prepare before asking for an offer?
sections.html:
Have a few basic facts ready so the first conversation can end with a clear next step.

  • Which school district the address falls in, since two districts split the city.
  • Whether the house is near Crow, Pigeon or Spencer creek, or has ever had water in the basement.
  • Whether the house is rented, and if so, whether it has a rental registration and an inspection certificate.
  • Which tax installments you have paid, and whether any are open.
  • The names on the deed and any mortgage payoff.

With those answers, the title company can tell us quickly whether the closing can be set for a date that suits you.

sections.h2: What does a Bettendorf cash sale look like?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Bettendorf skips the lender, so closing depends mostly on title work and your schedule.

  • You send the address and the condition of the house.
  • We review it and send a written offer, which you can accept or decline.
  • A title company prepares the deed, the declaration of value, and the groundwater hazard statement or its exemption sentence.
  • Because Bettendorf is in Scott County, the deed goes to the Scott County Recorder, whose recording page lists the transfer tax rule on the sale price over $500.

Property tax in Scott County is due in two installments, September 30 and March 31. Any open installment is settled at closing out of the sale proceeds.

faqs.q: Is flooding a concern in Bettendorf?
faqs.a: It can be. Wikipedia reports frequent flooding along the river and annual stormwater runoff, with Crow, Pigeon and Spencer creeks named as problem areas in a 2000 drainage study.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bettendorf house with a wet basement or other damage?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so you do not need to repair water damage first. Disclose known issues accurately.
